- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing upside.
- Model often overshoots after a sharp price spike; cap forecast 3–5 days after spike at 10–15% below peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to continue falling; add 2–5% upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently overestimates later days (especially 20–30d) — apply 3–5% downward correction for days 25–30.
- Sentiment volatility >0.2 in last 5 days → model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 2–3 days ahead.
